**Title:** TypeError When Setting Categorical Value in Single-Row DataFrame Using `.loc`

**Description:**
When attempting to set a categorical value for a column in a single-row DataFrame using the `.loc` indexer, a `TypeError` is raised due to an incorrect data type handling.

**Buggy Code Example:**
```python
import pandas as pd
from pandas import DataFrame, Series

# Create a single-row DataFrame
df = DataFrame({"Alpha": ["a"], "Numeric": [0]})

# Define categorical data with specific categories
categories = pd.Categorical(df["Alpha"], categories=["a", "b", "c"])

# Attempt to set the categorical value using .loc
df.loc[:, "Alpha"] = categories

# Retrieve the updated column
result = df["Alpha"]
expected = Series(categories, index=df.index, name="Alpha")
```

The path: when `arr_value.shape[0] == values.shape[0]` and sizes match, it sets values[indexer] = value (which converts to ndarray of the categorical's values) then tries `values.astype(arr_value.dtype)` which fails for extension dtypes.

entries.content: Fixed. Root cause: for a single-row DataFrame, `.loc[:, col] = value` went through `_setitem_with_indexer`'s split path, where `pi` is unwrapped from the tuple `(slice(None),)` to a bare `slice(None)`. The existing fast-path that replaces the whole column (`s = v`) only matched tuple indexers, so single-row frames fell into `Block.setitem`, which crashed at `values.astype(arr_value.dtype)` because numpy's `astype` doesn't understand `CategoricalDtype` (or any `ExtensionDtype`). The fix is two-fold: (1) in `pandas/core/indexing.py`, the null-slice check in `setter` now also matches a bare (non-tuple) null slice, so single-row full-column `.loc` assignment replaces the column — identical to the existing multi-row behavior — yielding the expected categorical column; (2) in `pandas/core/internals/blocks.py` `Block.setitem`, the exact-length-match `astype` is skipped for extension dtypes, eliminating the same `TypeError` on parallel paths (boolean-mask assignment, `Series.loc[:] = categorical`). Verified the issue example, edge cases (iloc, list/scalar assignment, datetime-tz EAs, partial setitem), and the full indexing/frame/series/internals test suites pass.
